description: The button on a customer's Contacts card that links a contact to the customer.
The button in the Add contact dialog that links the contact to the customer.
The field in the Add contact dialog where you find an existing contact or start a new one.
The name field of the customer form. For a business it looks the name up in the Brønnøysund register.
The button that saves the customer form.
The choice between a business and a private person in the new customer form.
The button above the customer list that opens the form for a new customer.
The button on a metering point's Supply periods card that starts a supply period for a customer.
The customer field of the supply period dialog.
The button in the supply period dialog that saves the supply period.
The date the supply period starts, in the supply period dialog.
The street address field in the new metering point form; the postal code, city and country follow it.
The GSRN field, the metering point's 18-digit number, in the new metering point form.
The meter number field in the new metering point form.
The button that saves the metering point form.
The button above the metering point list that opens the form for a new metering point.
The button on a travel claim that submits it for approval.
The description field of the expense form.
The button that saves the expense as a draft, from where it can be submitted.
The button on My expenses that opens the form for a new expense.
The button on My expenses that opens the form for a new travel claim.
The button on the Counts page that opens a stock count of a site, or of a location and everything below it.
The field at the top of the Inventory home page: scan or type a location code, a label, a SKU or a barcode and press Enter to open it.
The button on the Inventory home page that opens a new stock adjustment, to correct what lies on a location with a reason.
The button on the Inventory home page that opens a new move, to move stock between two locations of one site.
The button on the Inventory home page that opens a new goods receipt, to receive items onto a location.
The button on the Inventory home page that opens the form for a new site, a warehouse or a store.
The field on the Import page where the CSV of opening balances — location, sku and quantity — is chosen before a dry run.

The list on the Low stock page: every item at or below its reorder point at a site, filtered by site and searched by SKU or name, with what is available and incoming, the suggested quantity and how it was rounded up to whole packagings, and what other sites have. Choose rows at one site to create a transfer to it, or export the list as CSV.
The button on a site's page that creates a grid of locations at once, such as aisles, racks and shelves.
The button on a site's page that opens the form for a new location directly under the site.
The button on a site's page that downloads a PDF of location labels, for every location in the site or the ones chosen, on an Avery L7160 or L7163 sheet.
The field at the top of a transfer's receive page: each scan of a SKU or barcode counts one more on its line; the transfer note's barcode opens its transfer.
The list on the Transfers page: transfers of stock between sites, filtered by status (open by default), from site and to site, and searched by transfer number or SKU; an overdue transfer is marked.
The button on the Transfers page that opens a new transfer's draft: the from and to site, the lines, and the stock available at both sites beside each line.
The button below a draft invoice's lines that adds an empty line.
The button that issues a saved draft invoice and gives it its number.
The button that saves changes to a draft invoice.
The button in the new invoice dialog that creates the draft and opens it.
The customer picker of the new invoice dialog.
The button above the invoice list that starts a new invoice.
The components at standard cost, the operations' cost and their total, for someone who may see costs.
The quantity to explode the bill of materials at, and the site whose available stock is shown.
The exploded bill of materials: each component made or bought, what is required and the operations' expected time.
The buttons at the top of a bill of materials: its overview, make it the variant's default, archive or reactivate it.
The product variant the bill makes, its code, output quantity, lead time, make to order and note.
The components the product is made of: each one's quantity, scrap, the operation that consumes it and its order.
The operations in sequence: each one's work center, setup, minutes per cycle and instructions for the shop floor.
The button that saves the bill of materials with its operations and components.
The filters by status, code or product and variant, and the bills of materials they find.
The button on the Bills of materials page that opens the editor for a new one.
The cards at the top of the Manufacturing overview: active work centers, blocked work centers and active bills of materials.
The button on the Manufacturing overview that opens the editor for a new bill of materials.
The buttons at the top of a work center that archive, reactivate or delete it.
The days the work center is closed, such as an industrial holiday, and the fields to add one.
The work center's code, name, site, capacity, efficiency, setup and cleanup minutes and, for someone who may see costs, its cost rates.
The hours the work center is open each weekday: at most two intervals a day, in 15-minute steps.
The button that saves the work center.
The filters by status, site and code or name, and the work centers they find.
The button on the Work centers page that opens the form for a new work center.
Downloads the open view's table as a CSV file.
The tabs of the analysis: quote hit rate, order intake and backlog.
On the customer's Orders tab, starts a new order for this customer.
On the customer's Orders tab, starts a new quote for this customer.
Switches between the orders still to deliver (back orders) and the delivery documents.
Prints the delivery's lines sorted by location, with the locations holding each item.
Takes the stock off the chosen locations, registers the quantities delivered on the order and stores the packing slip.
On a posted delivery's Shipments card: proposes a shipment with one package weighing the delivered goods, on the site's default carrier account.
The customer's and the products' sales warnings, and for a settings holder the override of a block and the customer's warning.
Opens the variant grid: a product's variants by size and colour, with a quantity per cell, added as lines.
Adds a shipping line: the freight the customer pays, quantity 1, its price typed or estimated.
Asks the carrier for the shipping line's price for the delivery address and the goods' weight, with the markup from the settings.
Creates the draft order for the picked customer and opens its editor.
The customer picker a new order starts from.
Creates the draft quote for the picked customer and opens its editor.
The customer picker a new quote starts from.
Creates the draft subscription on the plan chosen and opens its editor.
The customer picker a new subscription starts from.
Confirms a draft order: freezes its prices and customer, and stores the order confirmation.
On a confirmed order's Deliveries card: makes a draft delivery of every open line at what is available at the site.
Saves an order's header and lines; a confirmed order takes changes to what is not delivered or invoiced.
The Inventory site the order is reserved and delivered from; shown while Inventory keeps stock.
The button above the order list that starts a new order.
Records that the customer accepted a sent quote and makes an order of it.
The accept dialog: the optional lines the customer took, and whether a draft or a confirmed order is made.
Saves a draft quote's header and lines; the server prices the lines and computes the totals.
Opens the send dialog that e-mails the quote's PDF to the customer and moves it to sent.
The button above the quote list that starts a new quote.
The Inventory site a new order is fulfilled from.
The final period a new subscription takes: the period the end falls in billed in full, or pro-rated to the end date.
The percent a shipping line's estimate adds to the carrier's price.
Saves the Orders settings: number series, validity, payment terms, the send channel and the mail texts.
Every customer's and product's sales warning, set, changed and removed here.
Books the shipment with the carrier, stores its label and waybill and, when the settings say so, e-mails the customer the tracking link.
The carrier's product the shipment is booked as, such as Bring's parcel to a pickup point.
Adds a Bring account: the Mybring user and API key, the customer numbers and whether it runs in test mode.
Checks the account's keys with the carrier and lists the services it can book; says when prices are list prices only.
Activates a draft subscription, so its periods are billed.
The period start an active subscription's line changes take effect from.
Sets the subscription's end; its period is the last one billed.
In the End dialog: bill the last period in full or pro-rated to the end date, pre-selected from the subscription's setting.
Whether the period the end falls in is billed in full or pro-rated to the end date; editable while the subscription runs.
Stops billing from a period start.
Restarts billing from a period start; the periods between are skipped.
Saves the subscription: a draft whole, an active one's lines from the period chosen.
The button above the subscription list that starts a new subscription.
Starts a new quote template with texts and lines a quote can start from.
The project code field; a suggestion is offered for it.
The customer picker of the project form; an internal project has no customer.
The name field of the project form.
The button that saves the project form.
The button above the project list that opens the form for a new project.
The button on the Day page that opens the form for a new time entry.
The hours field of the time entry form; it is worked out from the start and end time when both are filled in.
The project field of the time entry form.
The button that saves the time entry.
The button on My week that submits the week for approval.
